overall: New York City hit its daily peak of 98.1°F at 16:51 ET and has been cooling steadily for the past two hours, now sitting at 93.0°F with a velocity of -2.0°F/hr. Conditions are well past the diurnal maximum, with severe thunderstorm activity ongoing (active Warning through 8:30 PM and Watch through 11 PM), which will reinforce the cooling trend through the overnight hours. The day ran hotter than the NWS narrative forecast of 96°F, reflecting the intense heat event observed.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models (GFS=105.1°F, ECMWF=103.4°F, HRRR=100.4°F, NBM=100.4°F) all overshot significantly relative to the observed peak of 98.1°F, with HRRR and NBM being the closest but still running ~2.3°F high. The NWS text forecast of 96°F was itself underdone by about 2°F, suggesting the boundary layer mixed out hotter than expected before the afternoon thunderstorm convection limited further heating.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high is effectively locked in at 98.1°F — the temperature peaked 2 hours ago and the active severe weather environment eliminates any realistic path to a new high this evening. The INTRADAY model confirms 100% probability in the 98-99°F even bucket, consistent with the observed running max. Confidence is extremely high; the only residual uncertainty is a highly improbable convective outflow or measurement artifact, neither of which is supported by current data.
